stances.claim: The SC's TROs against Comelec Resolution No. 11044-A were warranted because the OMB dismissals carrying perpetual disqualification are still under appeal and therefore not final and enforceable -- a simple reason GEG himself acknowledged in conceding 'this is just a timely TRO.'
GEG further conceded that all ~100 candidates with non-final perpetual disqualifications should be included in the May 2025 ballot -- which CJ judges correct this time.

Per Macalintal's email clarification, the SC's affirmation of Rosal's disqualification refers to his 2022 gubernatorial candidacy, while the current TRO concerns the 2025 exercise -- distinguishing the two even though Rosal won Albay in 2022 with an overwhelming 230,735-vote majority against then-Gov Al Francis Bichara.

After CJ's Oct 14 hope that GEG would redeem himself, the multiple new TROs have made that hope 'evaporate' -- but CJ is not ready to knock GEG out because GEG has the more crucial job of assuring HOPE (Honest, Orderly, Peaceful) elections in 2025.

Beyond the usual 3Gs (guns, goons, gold), 2025 faces two new challenges: AI and the untested Miru System -- and GEG has rightly recognized AI's risks and required all candidates to register their online identities by Dec 13 (only 62 of 44,000+ had complied by Oct 23).

GEG's threat that endorsements via unregistered social-media outlets will be presumed candidate-owned and subject to disqualification or 1-6 years' imprisonment is forceful -- 'let's see whether the Comelec and GEG have the gravitas and the guts to enforce his big talk.'
Comelec's posting of party-list nominees' names for public scrutiny is a new requirement some may challenge, but the SC is likely to uphold the constitutional authority of the Comelec to assure HOPE.

The Miru System has never been tried locally and CJ cannot yet accept or reject it -- PPCRV and Namfrel should investigate, monitor, and critique; meanwhile, observing the Nov 5 US election will give the Comelec and the public an experiential view of how AI can be used, abused, and misused.

notable_anecdotes: The Tagalog editorial gloss -- 'Sana nga, pero hindi ginawa eh' (We should have done it but, regretfully, did not) -- one of the rare Tagalog phrases preserved in CJ's late columns, deployed to soften criticism of GEG with collegial familiarity.

The Macalintal aside -- 'who I know had declined an offer to be Comelec chair more than 10 years ago' -- a quiet credentialing of the email-correspondent that also underscores Macalintal's stature beyond the immediate case.
Rosal's 230,735-vote 2022 victory over Bichara cited as the political-cost backdrop of the disqualification -- turning a doctrinal disagreement into a story about voter mandate.

The 'evaporation' verb for hope -- 'Well, given these multiple TROs, my hope has just evaporated' -- uniquely vivid for CJ's measured register, and immediately followed by the refusal-to-knock-out posture.
The HOPE acronym (Honest, Orderly, Peaceful) -- quintessential CJ-style coinage compressing the Comelec's mandate into a four-letter framework.
The 62-of-44,000 social-media compliance datum -- used as the empirical pressure point on GEG's 'big talk' enforcement threat.
The Nov 5 US election treated as a real-time AI laboratory for Philippine 2025 -- explicit comparative-learning framing.

one_paragraph_summary: The Supreme Court issued temporary restraining orders against Comelec -- under chair George Erwin Garcia (GEG) -- stopping the implementation of Resolution No. 11044-A dated Sept 4, 2024, which had disqualified Mandaue City Mayor Jonas C. Cortes, former Albay Governor Noel E. Rosal, and Cebu City Mayor Michael L. Rama from 2025 candidacy based on Ombudsman dismissals carrying perpetual disqualification -- for the very simple reason that those OMB dismissals are still under appeal and therefore not final. GEG himself conceded the TRO was 'timely' ('Sana nga, pero hindi ginawa eh' -- we should have done it but did not) and rightly added that all ~100 such non-final disqualified candidates should be on the May 2025 ballot. The SC's Oct 22, 2024 press release affirming Rosal's disqualification, CJ clarifies via Romulo Macalintal's email, refers to Rosal's 2022 gubernatorial candidacy (won with an overwhelming 230,735-vote majority against then-Gov Al Francis Bichara), while the current TRO is for 2025. After CJ's Oct 14 column expressed hope that GEG would redeem himself, the multiple new TROs have made that hope 'evaporate' -- but CJ refuses to knock him out because GEG faces the more crucial job of assuring HOPE (Honest, Orderly, Peaceful) elections in 2025. Beyond the usual 3Gs (guns, goons, gold), two new challenges loom: artificial intelligence and the untested Miru System. GEG has required all candidates to register their online identities by Dec 13 (only 62 of over 44,000 had complied as of Oct 23) and forcefully threatened disqualification or 1-6 years' imprisonment for endorsements via unregistered social-media outlets -- 'let's see whether the Comelec and GEG have the gravitas and the guts to enforce his big talk.' Comelec's posting of party-list nominees' names for public scrutiny may be challenged, but the SC is likely to uphold Comelec's constitutional authority to assure HOPE. The Nov 5 US presidential election will give the Comelec and the Filipino public an experiential view of how AI can be used, abused, and misused; the Miru System remains untested locally, and CJ leaves its investigation, monitoring, and critique to PPCRV and Namfrel.
